truthAudit.Summary: Audited Run 2 against the 20 supplied truth vulnerabilities. The previous answer fully or partially covered 16 items and missed 4. It also contained out-of-truth findings and several severity or CWE overclaims that are corrected below.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format string injection from configurable log format
Items.Notes: Previous answer explicitly identified runtime_log_format and printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) as a format string vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Factorial function allows unbounded loop and integer overflow
Items.Notes: Previous answer identified the fact loop and result *= i as causing signed integer overflow, though it under-rated severity and used the wrong CWE.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free in deferred history flush during cleanup
Items.Notes: Previous answer identified scratch memory being read by enqueued tasks after memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup, matching the truth use-after-free.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command injection through validator_path in validate_config
Items.Notes: Previous answer identified validator_cmd + config_file passed to system in validate_config, matching the truth command injection via config validation.
Previous answer identified strcpy(input_buffer_, expression.c_str()) for long expressions as a stack buffer overflow, but overclaimed severity and used a generic CWE.
Previous answer identified value_ being read outside the mutex before lock_guard and then updated, matching the truth race condition.
Previous answer identified login_attempts_ > 5 followed by EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE setting authenticated_ = true, but overclaimed severity and used the wrong CWE.
Previous answer identified config_dir_ + filename in load_config and admin load as path traversal.
Previous answer identified the 256-byte expression_buffer_ and strcpy of a potentially longer token string, matching the truth heap overflow.
Previous answer identified ADMIN_SECRET and SC_ENT_2025_AUTH as hardcoded administrator credentials.
Previous answer identified std::mt19937 and uniform_int_distribution 1000 to 9999 as weak session token generation, but under-rated severity.
Previous answer did not identify the static std::tm cached_time and localtime update in log_debug_message as a thread-unsafe timestamp cache.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command injection in emergency override audit logging
Items.Notes: Previous answer identified the same append_override_audit_event code using TEMP or TMPDIR, supercalc_emergency.log, and system, but framed it as command injection rather than the truth insecure temporary file handling issue.
Previous answer did not identify persistent authentication state involving authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ as a distinct weakness.
Previous answer identified std::stod(tokens[3]) in handle_variable_command as an unhandled exception source.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Memory pool split size underflow leads to out-of-bounds allocation
Items.Notes: Previous answer identified previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES underflow and fragment.size = remaining, matching the truth integer underflow.
Previous answer did not identify unbounded recursion through parse_expression, parse_term, and parse_factor with PAREN_OPEN as a stack exhaustion or unbounded recursion weakness.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race in expression result cache
Items.Notes: Previous answer identified unlocked result_cache_ access in evaluate_cached while thread pool tasks can call it concurrently, matching the truth data race.
Previous answer did not identify the TOCTOU window between std::filesystem::exists, sleep_for, and std::ifstream in load_config.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer division by zero in route score calculation
Items.Notes: Previous answer identified 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length) with token_length possibly zero, but overclaimed severity.
